You are an experienced NSW HSC Business Studies marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2020 NSW HSC Business Studies exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 24(d) [4 marks]: Explain TWO ways in which comparative ratio analysis can be used by this business to assess its financial position.
STIMULUS / CASE INFORMATION:
Financial Information for robotics company

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 4):
4 marks: Provides an explanation of how TWO ways of comparative ratio analysis can be used to assess the financial position of the business
3 marks: Sketches in general terms how TWO ways of comparative ratio analysis can be used to assess the financial position of the business
2 marks: Sketches in general terms how comparative ratio analysis can be used to assess the financial position of the business
1 marks: Sketches comparative ratio analysis in general terms

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
First method is over different time periods. This business could be comparing financial data within different years or financial periods to analyse liquidity, gearing, profitability and efficiency and to understand how these have changed and put strategies in place to address any issues. The second way is against similar businesses. This business could see the financial position of the competition to understand if their expenses are too high compared to competitors. If this is the case, then the business could change their supplier to a cheaper one. Also, if the competitor has consistently made sales, even during slow periods, the business can analyse this to understand what they are doing wrong and hence make adjustments.



WHAT THE REAL MARKERS SAID ABOUT THIS QUESTION:
Better responses: engage with the stimulus material to correctly calculate key financial ratios using the correct units
Better responses: demonstrate their understanding of comparative ratio analysis by interpreting how the selected business compares to the industry standard
Better responses: assess business performance using comparative ratio analysis
Better responses: recommend and explain valid strategies to improve financial performance.
To improve: understanding place value when calculating ratios and using the correct units associated with each ratio
To improve: demonstrating a clear understanding of key financial ratios and their interpretation.

STUDENT RESPONSE:
